name: Sermorelin
used_for: Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of growth hormone-releasing hormone. Drugs@FDA shows Geref (sermorelin acetate) was approved under NDA 019863 (1990) and NDA 020443 (1997), but both are now listed as discontinued, and openFDA/Drugs@FDA show no currently marketed sermorelin product. FDA published a 2013 notice that Geref was not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons. Today it is mainly promoted by anti-aging and telehealth clinics, usually as a compounded product, to raise growth hormone for body composition, sleep and energy in adults. The published human work found here is small and older, mostly in children with growth hormone deficiency and in healthy volunteers.

entries.text: GHRH(1-29)-NH2 (the sermorelin sequence) at 30 or 60 micrograms/kg/day, given as a continuous infusion for 6 months. Height growth was lower than with growth hormone (9.2 and 9.3 versus 14.6 cm/year).
entries.population: 60 children with growth hormone deficiency of hypothalamic origin

entries.text: GHRH(1-29)-NH2 single intravenous doses of 0.25 to 2 micrograms/kg raised growth hormone (maximal at 1 to 2 micrograms/kg); intranasal dosing needed about 50 micrograms/kg for a similar effect.

internet_entries.text: An educational website (Peptide Dossier) says most sermorelin protocols begin with 200 mcg daily, increased to 300 mcg after 1 to 2 weeks, with 300 to 500 mcg daily described for experienced users. The site says it does not encourage use without medical supervision.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: A compounded-peptide telehealth seller says the typical adult range is 200 to 500 mcg injected subcutaneously once daily at bedtime, with 100 to 200 mcg described as a conservative starting level. The page is part of a site that sells the product.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: The Peptidepedia website says sermorelin is injected 15 to 30 minutes before bed on an empty stomach, at least 90 minutes after eating, and that a mixed vial is refrigerated and used within 4 to 6 weeks, with a vial left unrefrigerated for more than 72 hours to be discarded.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: A telehealth clinic blog (Defy Medical) says a reconstituted sermorelin vial is kept refrigerated and can last up to 90 days, and can tolerate under 72 hours out of the fridge. It describes injecting slowly under the skin of the abdomen, arm, thigh or buttock and rotating sites. The clinic sells sermorelin therapy.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: A 1999 review states that in children with idiopathic growth hormone deficiency, once daily subcutaneous sermorelin was given at bedtime in the treatment studies it covered.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Peptidepedia website says sermorelin is injected into the abdomen, front of the thigh or back of the upper arm with rotation, that 15 to 30 minutes before bed lines up with the early slow-wave-sleep growth hormone pulse, that daytime use is said to be less effective, and that reconstituted vials should never be frozen.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In a 6-month trial in children with growth hormone deficiency, no serious side effects were seen; three children receiving GHRH(1-29)-NH2 reported mild injection site irritation.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the same trial, nearly all children given GHRH(1-29)-NH2 (39 of 40) developed antibodies to it, which had almost disappeared 9 months after treatment stopped; no correlation with growth response was found.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: A clinic blog says sermorelin is better than hormone replacement because it stimulates natural growth hormone release, and lists benefits including more muscle, less fat, better sleep, faster healing and heart health.
Testing.com says human evidence for sermorelin's anti-aging benefits is limited, that most claimed effects are anecdotal, and that compounded sermorelin is not an FDA-approved product.

A health-system blog says there is no FDA-approved sermorelin product on the US market, that old small studies showed only modest changes, that no randomized trial shows better sleep or strength, and that growth hormone in healthy older adults caused swelling and joint pain.

research.summary: Drugs@FDA overview page for NDA 020443 (Geref, sermorelin acetate 0.5 mg and 1 mg vials).
research.finding: Lists the original approval date of 09/26/1997 and shows both Geref products with marketing status Discontinued, with a note that FDA determined the product was not discontinued or withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons.

research.summary: FDA notice published in the Federal Register on March 4, 2013 (Docket FDA-2012-P-1071).
research.finding: FDA determined Geref injection (0.5 mg and 1.0 mg vials, and 0.05 mg ampule) was not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness, which would allow FDA to approve generic applications that meet other requirements. It does not approve any product.

research.summary: Randomized 6-month comparison of GHRH(1-29)-NH2 (30 or 60 micrograms/kg/day) versus growth hormone in 60 children with growth hormone deficiency (Chen et al., Acta Paediatr Suppl).
research.finding: Growth with GHRH(1-29)-NH2 was clearly less than with growth hormone. Nearly all treated children developed antibodies to GHRH, and the authors concluded it was unlikely to be as effective as growth hormone for growth.

research.summary: Pharmacokinetic and hormone-response study of GHRH(1-29)-NH2 given intravenously or intranasally to 30 healthy men (Wilton et al., Acta Paediatr Suppl).
research.finding: Intravenous doses released growth hormone, which stayed elevated for about 3 hours; nasal absorption was low (3 to 5% bioavailability). This is a short-term study in healthy men and does not show clinical benefit.

research.summary: Review of sermorelin in the diagnosis and treatment of children with idiopathic growth hormone deficiency (Prakash and Goa, BioDrugs), covering the treatment trials.
research.finding: The review states that once daily subcutaneous sermorelin given at bedtime was effective in some prepubertal children with idiopathic growth hormone deficiency, based on limited data.
